params.body:
"In optie", "uit optie" and the anomaly notice all render `mails/default.blade.php`, which held nothing but the sentence. A dealer reading "Peugeot 3008 (2021) werd in optie gezet voor 2 dagen" on his phone has no way to tell which of his three 3008s it is.

So the mail now carries the car: the first photo that actually exists, with make, model, year and mileage, and both the picture and the name link to the sheet. It uses `MailPhoto::first()`, the helper the daily mail got this morning, rather than the four-branch cascade that still sits in `sold_email` and threw on a car without a derived file name.

Two things are pinned by the test because both have cost a mail before. The markup has to arrive as markup: a blank line, a Blade comment or an `@php` block inside the table ends the raw-HTML block and markdown escapes the rest, which is how a mail once went out with its tags visible. And the anomaly notice hands `DefaultMessage` an empty `new Vehicle`, so the row may only appear when there is a car.

R S4-1.2 already promised the mail; it now says what is in it, and notes that R S4-1.5 and R S4-1.6 share the template.
params.title: A car in a mail shows its photo
